messages.content: You check each debater against its own earlier words. You bring nothing from outside the words given to you: no doctrine, no training knowledge, no reading of your own. You do not judge who is right, and you do not judge one side by the other side's words.

You are the closing enforcer. A debater's closing round may not contradict what the same debater stated in its earlier rounds. Below are one debater's four rounds.
Read its closing round against its earlier rounds. List every closing sentence that cannot be true together with an earlier sentence, and answer every candidate listed.
A contradiction is two statements that cannot both be true. A closing sentence that asserts again, as the debater's own, what it withdrew, dropped or gave up in an earlier round IS a contradiction.
It is NOT a contradiction when the closing sentence: grants, concedes, narrows or withdraws something; states or quotes the other side's position; answers a press with a further reason the earlier sentence leaves room for; or differs only in wording.
Quote both sentences word for word and name the link: the link whose closing block holds the sentence, else the link the earlier sentence supports.
Reply with one line per contradiction and per candidate, and nothing else:
CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: <candidate id or NEW> -- <DEFENDER|CHALLENGER> -- LINK <n> -- CONFIRMED | NOT A CONTRADICTION -- EARLIER [<round>] "<words>" -- CLOSING [<round 4>] "<words>" -- <one sentence: why both cannot be true, or why they can>
If you find none and there is no candidate, reply: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NONE

CANDIDATES ALREADY NAMED (answer each one by its id):
A49 -- DEFENDER -- LINK (you name it) -- EARLIER [CR2] "I do not press it as a correction" -- CLOSING [CR4] "The household word is used, and the child at once names another Father." -- named by the anti-cheat check: Luke 2:49

######## THE DEFENDER ########
The defender's links: D1 = LINK 1, D2 = LINK 2, D3 = LINK 3, D4 = LINK 4, D5 = LINK 5, D6 = LINK 6 (its DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1]). Its closing round is [CR4].

=== [CR1] ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** I defend the standard reading. Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no human male as begetter. Joseph was his legal and household father, not his biological father. I use "biological father" to mean the man whose seed begets a child.

---

## 1. The genealogy changes its verb and its source at Jesus

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] The verb "begat" is *egennēsen* (G1080, gennaō, "to beget, to father"), in the active voice with a male subject. It is used through the whole list. In verse 16 the active "begat" ends at Joseph, who is called "the husband of Mary". Jesus is then "born" by *egennēthē* (G1080, passive: "was begotten/born"). The relative "of whom" is *ex hēs* (G1537 + feminine singular, "out of whom, her"). The Greek grammar makes Mary alone the source named for Jesus. In the rest of the chain the source is the male.

[L3] Matthew 1:18 gives the reason for the change: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:2 and 1:16 [L1], plus the feminine *ex hēs* [L2]. The list uses the male verb "begat" for every father and changes to a passive verb with a feminine source at Jesus. So Matthew marks the line as running through a husband, not a begetter, at this one point.

## 2. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know"), in Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25, is the Greek word that carries the sense of marital knowledge. *Parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") is the word in Luke 1:27. *Synelthein* (G4905, "to come together") in Matthew 1:18 puts the conception before any coming together.

[L3] Genesis 4:1 gives the same idiom: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain."

[L4] Footing: Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:18 [L1], plus *ginōskō* [L2], which Genesis 4:1 [L3] shows leading to conception. Mary says she has not known a man. Matthew says the conception was found before the coming together. Matthew 1:25 says Joseph did not know her until after the birth. So no man's knowing of her stands behind the conception.

## 3. The text names the source of the conception, and it is the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] In Matthew 1:20 the preposition is *ek* (G1537, "out of"), which marks source. *Gennēthen* (G1080, "that which is begotten/conceived") is passive, so the one begotten has a source named. In Luke 1:35 *epeleusetai* (G1904, "shall come upon") and *episkiasei* (G1982, "shall overshadow") describe the action. *Dio* (G1352, "wherefore, therefore") ties his being called the Son of God to this conception.

[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me." *Katērtisō* (G2675, "to fit, to prepare") says the body was prepared by God.

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:20 with *ek* [L2], and Luke 1:35 with *dio* [L2], supported by Hebrews 10:5 [L3]. The verses name "the Holy Ghost" as the source of what is conceived, and the angel gives that as the ground of the title. The ground for the title is stated as the Holy Ghost's act, and no human male is named as source. This leaves no place for a biological human father.

## 4. "Father" said of Joseph is reckoned or legal, not generative

[L1] Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

[L2] *Enomizeto* (G3543, "was reckoned, was supposed") is the verb behind "as was supposed". Luke marks the sonship as a matter of reckoning.

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

[L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

[L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?"

[L3] Luke 2:48 and 2:49 set two fathers side by side. Mary says "thy father" of Joseph. Jesus answers with "my father's business", which the same passage puts in the temple of God. The word "father" is used of Joseph in the household sense and is then corrected by the child's own use of it.

[L4] Footing: Luke 3:23 with *enomizeto* [L2], and Luke 2:48-49 [L3]. Luke qualifies Joseph's fatherhood as "supposed", and the child himself redirects "father" to another. Joseph's fatherhood is therefore the fatherhood of the household and the supposition of others, not begetting.

## 5. Prophecy: the seed of the woman and the virgin's conception

[L1] Genesis 3:15: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."

[L2] *Zera'* (H2233, "seed") is attached to "the woman" here. [L3] Genesis 16:10 also speaks of a woman's seed: "I will multiply thy seed exceedingly." So Scripture can speak of seed through a woman.

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

[L2] *'Almah* (H5959) is the Hebrew word the KJV renders "virgin".

[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

[L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:14 [L1] with H5959 [L2], and Matthew 1:23 [L1] as the application. Genesis 3:15 [L3] supports the same pattern, since it speaks of a seed attached to the woman. The prophecy names a virgin conceiving and bearing, and Matthew 1:23 applies it to Mary's conception. The same pattern is given at the first promise, with the seed reckoned to the woman.

**On Romans 1:3.** [L1] Romans 1:3 says Christ "was made of the seed of David according to the flesh". [L2] *Ek spermatos* (G1537 + G4690, "out of the seed") and *kata sarka* (G2596 + G4561, "according to the flesh") state descent in the flesh from David. [L3] Genesis 16:10 shows seed spoken of through a woman. So descent from David through Mary's flesh answers Romans 1:3 without a human begetter. Mary is of the house of David on the plain statement of Luke 1:27, where the "house of David" stands in the same verse as "the virgin's name was Mary". [L4] Footing: Romans 1:3 with G4690 [L2], and Genesis 16:10 [L3].

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew's genealogy uses the active "begat" for every father and then gives Jesus as "born" of Mary alone; footing: [L1] Matthew 1:2 and Matthew 1:16, [L2] *egennēsen*/*egennēthē* (G1080) and the feminine *ex hēs* (G1537).
2. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man, and the conception came before Joseph and Mary came together; footing: [L1] Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:18, [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") with [L3] Genesis 4:1.
3. The source of the conception is stated to be the Holy Ghost, and that conception is the ground of the title Son of God; footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, [L2] *ek* (G1537, "out of") and *dio* (G1352, "therefore"), [L3] Hebrews 10:5.
4. Joseph's fatherhood is reckoned and household fatherhood, not begetting; footing: [L1] Luke 3:23, [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed"), [L3] Luke 2:48-49.
5. The prophecy of a virgin conceiving, applied by Matthew to Mary, with seed reckoned through the woman, agrees with links 1 to 4; footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23, [L2] *'almah* (H5959, the word rendered "virgin"), [L3] Genesis 3:15.
6. Christ had no biological father; he was conceived by the Holy Ghost in the virgin Mary, and Joseph was his father only by reckoning and marriage; footing: links 1 to 5, resting on [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:34-35 with [L2] *ek* (G1537) and *ginōskō* (G1097).

=== [CR2] ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

# ROUND 2: DEFENDER'S ANSWER

I keep the opening chain and answer each press by its witness. Where a sentence of mine floated or overreached, I narrow it first.

---

## 0. Narrowings

- **Luke 1:27.** I withdraw "on the plain statement of Luke 1:27" for Mary's Davidic descent. The words "of the house of David" can attach to "a man whose name was Joseph." Mary's descent is carried below as an [L4] on other rows (§7).
- **Genesis 3:15 and 16:10.** The challenger is right that Genesis 4:25 gives Eve's "another seed" a father in Adam, and Genesis 16:15 gives Hagar's a father in Abram. I withdraw "seed reckoned to the woman" as proof of anything. Genesis 3:15 stands only as consistent with links 1-3 and carries no weight of its own.
- **Luke 2:49.** I do not press it as a correction of Mary's "thy father." Link 4 rests on Luke 3:23 and on Matthew 1:19-25.

---

## 1. The keystone, C4: "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal"

**(a) The order of the narrative.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L1] Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife."
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *Synerchomai* (G4905) in 1:18 is glossed "to cohabit (conjugally)." *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") in 1:25 is the word of Genesis 4:1 that the challenger himself cites. *Heōs* (G2193, "until") sets the limit at the birth.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The conception already stands when the angel speaks, and it is before the taking of 1:24.
- [L4] Joseph knew her not until the birth (1:25). The conception lies before the birth and before the taking (1:18, 1:20, 1:24). So the knowing that Genesis 4:1 gives as the means of conceiving cannot be placed in the span that Matthew 1:25 closes against it. C4 needs a knowing inside the espousal. Matthew 1:18 puts the finding of the child before any "coming together." Matthew 1:25 denies any knowing before the birth.

**(b) Joseph's own reaction (the press on Matthew 1:19).**
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24, the challenger's own row: the betrothed damsel and "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife" are brought to the gate and stoned.
- [L2] *Paradeigmatizō* (G3856, "to make a public example") is the public shaming of a wife found with child.
- [L4] A husband who knew himself the father would have no cause to think of a "publick example" or of putting her away. Joseph's plan is the plan of a just man who finds his betrothed wife with child by another and who is "not willing" to expose her. The challenger's own Deuteronomy 22:24 shows what that exposure would be. Then the angel's "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (1:20) tells him the source is "of the Holy Ghost," not another man. If Joseph knew he was the father, the plan of 1:19 is unexplained. The conception is therefore not his.

---

## 2. D1: Matthew 1:3, 1:5, 1:6 beside 1:16

- [L1] Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." Matthew 1:5: "Booz begat Obed of Ruth." Matthew 1:6: "David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias."
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- [L2] In 1:3, 1:5 and 1:6 the active *egennēsen* (G1080, "begat") has the man as subject, and *ek* (G1537, "out of") then adds the mother. In 1:16 the man in the *ek*-clause's neighbourhood is not a subject of "begat." He is *anēr* (G435, "man, husband"), "the husband of Mary," and the verb for Jesus is the passive *egennēthē* (G1080) with the feminine *hēs* ("of whom"). The pressed rows have a begetting man in the same clause as the *ek*-woman. Matthew 1:16 has a husband, and the born one is "of whom," feminine.
- [L3] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise." [L2] *Gennēsis* (G1083, "birth," from the same root as G1080) and *houtōs* (G3779, "in this way, referring to what follows") introduce a manner of birth that Matthew then sets out: "found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20, with the KJV margin "[conceived: Gr. begotten]." The verb of 1:20 is G1080, the verb of the genealogy's "begat" in Matthew 1:2. In the genealogy the begotten one has a man as source. In 1:20 the source is "of the Holy Ghost."
- [L4] Matthew 1:3-6 show *ek* with the mother where a man's "begat" is in the clause. Matthew 1:16 drops that "begat" at Joseph, and 1:18-20 supply the manner of birth and the source of the begotten one. So the pressed rows show the list's usual pattern and do not meet this exception. This answers Unsupported-L4 No. 1.

**On Matthew 1:1 (the list's purpose).**
- [L1] Matthew 1:1: "the son of David."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS."
- [L4] The angel addresses Joseph as son of David and charges him to take her and to name the child, and Joseph does both (1:24-25). Matthew's "son of David" is carried by Joseph's taking and naming. This is a reckoned line through the husband (see §6, Ezra 2:61).

---

## 3. D2: Luke 1:34 in the present tense

- [L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *Pōs* (G4459, "how, in what manner") asks the manner of a conceiving still future. *Ginōskō* (G1097) is in the present, so it is her state when she asks.
- [L3] Luke 1:27: she is "a virgin espoused" to Joseph, and she knows it.
- [L4] If the manner were a husband's knowing after the wedding, "how" would not need asking. The espousal already gave that manner. She asks "how" because her present state, "I know not a man," is set against the conceiving. The question names the manner and the answer meets it.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." This is the angel's reply to "How shall this be?" The reply names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and no man. This answers Unsupported-L4 No. 2.

---

## 4. D3: *ek* with God, and *dio kai*

**On John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1.**
- [L1] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- [L2] The same *ek* (G1537) stands in each clause. It sets *haima* (G129, "blood"), *thelēma sarkos* (G2307 + G4561, "will of flesh") and *thelēma andros* (G2307 + G435, "will of a man") against "of God." Here "of God" is the source that stands in the place of blood, flesh and a man's will.
- [L3] 1 John 5:1: "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." God is the one who "begat."
- [L4] The challenger's own rows use "of God" as a begetter set against a man's will, and the "begat" word (G1080) is used there. They do not support *ek* plus the Spirit as covenant title only. Matthew 1:20 uses G1080 with "of the Holy Ghost" in the same way. I hold that Jesus is not a believer born by faith, and Matthew 1:20 says "conceived in her" in the flesh. The rows show the pattern, a begotten one whose source is God and not man's will.

**On *dio kai* (G1352 + G2532).**
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *Dio* (G1352, "wherefore") has its ground in the clause just before it, in the same verse: the coming upon and the overshadowing. *Hagion* (G40, "holy") is the thing "born of thee."
- [L3] Luke 1:32 gives the title first. Luke 1:35 gives its ground, and the ground is not a covenant word but the Holy Ghost's coming upon her.
- [L4] The challenger's source for the title is 2 Samuel 7:14, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son," which is given beside David, Solomon's named father, and is conditioned: "If he commit iniquity." Luke 1:35's ground is the event of the conception. The overshadowing is "the power of the Highest" (G1411, "power"), and I agree that these are verbs of power. The power is what stands where a begetter would. This answers Unsupported-L4 No. 3.

**On Hebrews 10:5, 2:14 and 2:16.**
- [L1] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." [L2] *Katartizō* (G2675, "to fit, to frame"), with Hebrews 11:3 "framed by the word of God" [L3], has God as the one who fits the body.
- [L1] Hebrews 2:16: "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham."
- [L4] I grant that the body is of the seed of Abraham. This is no conflict. *Sperma* (G4690) in Hebrews 2:16 is posterity across forty generations, and Hebrews 7:5 shows the same reach (§6). It does not name Joseph as the begetter.

---

## 5. D4: *enomizeto*

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] *Nomizō* (G3543) is glossed "to accustom ... by extension, to deem or regard." It has both senses, and the context picks.
- [L1] Acts 14:19: "having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead."
- [L1] Acts 7:25: "For he supposed his brethren would have understood ... but they understood not."
- [L2] Both rows use G3543 in the "deem" sense, and in both the opinion did not hold: Paul was not dead, and the brethren did not understand.
- [L3] Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made," is the "custom" sense. The challenger is right that the word has it.
- [L4] Luke 3:23 sets "(as was supposed)" in a parenthesis before "the son of Joseph," between Jesus and the line. With Luke 1:34-35 just before it, and with the two rows where G3543 means a supposition that failed, the parenthesis marks the opinion of those who reckon, not a verdict on begetting by Luke's own voice. I hold the weight of link 4 on Matthew 1:19-25 together with Luke 3:23. This answers Unsupported-L4 No. 4.

**On the four voices (C2).**
- [L1] John 6:42: "whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?"
- [L4] The voices are the town's, Mary's, the disciple's and the angel's address. Each uses Joseph's name with the household relation or with David, and each is consistent with the reckoned line. The town's "we know" is a claim of theirs, and the same verse sets it against the child's own words. The rows state the household relation, and none states the begetting.

---

## 6. C1 and C3, and the question

**C1: "fruit of his loins."**
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ."
- [L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."
- [L3] Hebrews 7:5: "they come out of the loins of Abraham." Hebrews 7:9: "Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham."
- [L2] *Osphys* (G3751, "loin") in these rows spans generations. Levi is "in the loins" of Abraham, and Levi's sons "come out of" those loins. The word carries the line of descent from the forefather and does not mark the last begetter.
- [L4] Acts 2:30 swears the fruit of David's loins "according to the flesh" (*kata sarka*, G2596 + G4561). That is satisfied by flesh descended from David, and Hebrews 7:5-10 show the "loins" idiom over many generations. C1 needs the last link to be Joseph's loins, and neither row says so. It takes the C4 premise, which §1 answers.

**Joseph's line and Jechonias.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:11: "Josias begat Jechonias." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Joseph is in the "begat" line that runs through him.
- [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- [L3] Jeremiah 22:24: "Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah." Jeremiah 27:20: "Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah." These are the same man with the same father and the same title.
- [L4] The "begat" line that ends at Joseph runs through Jechonias. A son who sits on David's throne and is of Joseph's seed meets the word of Jeremiah 22:30. So Joseph as begetter strains the throne promise. Matthew 1:16 names Joseph "the husband," and the reckoned line gives the throne.

**D6 (Mary's descent).**
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli." Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph." Luke 3:31 includes "Nathan, which was" in the chain to David.
- [L3] Ezra 2:61: a man "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai ... and was called after their name."
- [L4] One man has one begetter. Matthew's line says Jacob begat Joseph, so Luke's Heli line reckons Joseph by something other than begetting. Ezra 2:61 is a KJV row where a man is called after his wife's father's house. I hold Mary's Davidic flesh as an inference: Luke 3:31's chain runs to David by Nathan, and "according to the flesh" in Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 is met there. This is an [L4] resting on two or more rows, and it is not stated by a single verse. It answers Unsupported-L4 No. 6.

**The question: how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14)?**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L2] *Anatellō* (G393, "to arise, to spring up") with *ek* (G1537) names the source tribe. The verse does not name a register.
- [L3] Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers," is the register of those numbered. Ezra 2:61-62, the challenger's own row, shows a man "called after" his wife's father's name and put to the register, so the register is not a proof of begetting.
- [L4] Two lines meet in "evident": Joseph's house by his taking and naming of the child (Matthew 1:20-21, 1:24-25, and Luke 2:4's "of the house and lineage of David"), and the flesh by Mary as above. Numbers 1:18 is the rule for numbering and does not state how a born child is reckoned when the husband takes him, and Ezra 2:61 shows a reckoning by the wife's house.

---

## 7. D5: Isaiah 7:14

- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
- [L2] *'Almah* (H5959) is the word in Isaiah 7:14.
- [L1] Isaiah 8:3: "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son." The child is called "Mahershalalhashbaz," and the Lord names it. In 7:14 the name is "Immanuel."
- [L1] Matthew 1:22-23: "that it might be fulfilled ... a virgin shall be with child ... God with us."
- [L2] *Parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") is Matthew's word, and Luke 1:27 uses it of Mary.
- [L4] Isaiah 8:3 has a different child with a different name, and the woman is "the prophetess," not "virgin." Matthew 1:22 gives the fulfilment, and Matthew 1:25 keeps her not known until the birth, so the "virgin ... with child" stands through the conception. The challenger's Isaiah 7:16 boundary names the sign's time and does not give a man. The pattern of 8:3 is a different row. This answers Unsupported-L4 No. 5, and I hold link 5 only as agreeing with links 1-4.

---

## 8. Chain after narrowing

- Link 1: held on Matthew 1:16, 1:18 and 1:20, with §2 as the answer to Matthew 1:3-6.
- Link 2: held on Matthew 1:18-19, 1:25 and Luke 1:34-35.
- Link 3: held on Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, with *dio* grounded in the verse's own clause.
- Link 4: narrowed to Luke 3:23 with Matthew 1:19-25.
- Link 5: held as agreement only, with Genesis 3:15 dropped as proof.
- Link 6: Christ had no biological father. He was conceived by the Holy Ghost in Mary, who had not known a man, and Joseph is his father by marriage and the naming of the child.

=== [CR3] ===
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

## LINK 1: NARROWED TO: Matthew's list carries the father's verb "begat" down to Jacob and Joseph, and the source Matthew names for the child's begetting is the Holy Ghost

I grant that Matthew 1:3, 1:5 and 1:6 pair "of" plus the mother with a begetting father. I withdraw any claim that the *ek*-form of itself sets the father aside.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate, properly of the father, but by extension of the mother"; glossed "beget, be born, conceive") is the one verb in both forms. *anēr* (G435, "man; husband") is Joseph's title in 1:16.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]". The list's own verb is given to the Holy Ghost as source.
- **[L4]** Resting on Matthew 1:16 and 1:20 [L1], *gennaō* [L2] and the margin at 1:20 [L3]:
  - The father's verb runs from Abraham through "Jacob begat Joseph".
  - Matthew 1:16 gives Joseph the title "the husband of Mary" and gives the birth as "of whom was born Jesus".
  - Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 then give the begetting to the Holy Ghost.

**Matthew 1:21 and Luke 1:62 (the naming press).**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:60: "And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:31 is said to Mary: "and shalt call his name JESUS". Genesis 4:25: "she bare a son, and called his name Seth".
- **[L4]** Naming is done by mothers in the very passages pressed, so the naming at Matthew 1:21 carries no begetting. Matthew 1:25, "he called his name JESUS", places the child in the line of Joseph, "thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). That is a reckoning, not a begetting.

**Matthew 1:1.** I grant that the list delivers "the son of David". It does so by Joseph's legal line (Matthew 1:20, 2:4 as the challenger holds). That does not touch the begetting of 1:20.

## LINK 2: NARROWED TO: the finding of the pregnancy is dated before "they came together" (Matthew 1:18), so the conception did not come by their coming together

I withdraw the claim that the span of 1:25 reaches back before the taking. I grant that it begins at 1:24.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** *synerchomai* (G4905, "to convene... or, specially, cohabit (conjugally)") is the "came together". It names the knowing of Genesis 4:1.
- **[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." The knowing comes first. Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife", so the taking is still ahead when the angel speaks.
- **[L4]** Resting on Matthew 1:18 [L1], *synerchomai* [L2] and Genesis 4:1 and Matthew 1:20 [L3]:
  - Joseph is "husband" in law from the espousal (Deuteronomy 22:24, granted).
  - But 1:18 separates "espoused" from "came together" and dates the child's being found before the latter.
  - The Genesis 4:1 means, the coming together, was not in place when she was "found with child of the Holy Ghost".

**Luke 1:34-36 and 1:13.**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The answer to it is Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:36 describes Elisabeth as one "who was called barren". Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- **[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is present in 1:34. *syllambanō* (G4815, "to conceive") is future in 1:31.
- **[L4]** The question is the means. The answer gives the Holy Ghost and power. The sign of Elisabeth is a sign of the impossible, shown in a barren woman, and it is attached to 1:35 by "also" in 1:36.

## LINK 3: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:18, 1:20 and Luke 1:35 give the conceiving to the Holy Ghost, and John 1:13 sets birth "of God" against "the will of man"

- **[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) here is "to regenerate" (figuratively). *thelēma* (G2307, "will, volition") is in "the will of man".
- **[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me".
- **[L4]** Resting on John 1:13 [L1], *gennaō* and *thelēma* [L2] and John 3:6 and Hebrews 10:5 [L3]:
  - The challenger's rows show a second birth beside a first.
  - But John 1:13 sets the birth "of God" against "of the will of man" in the one verse.
  - The same verb at Matthew 1:20 is said of the one conceived "in her", with no flesh birth beside it. Matthew 1:18 puts the finding before "they came together".

**Luke 1:35 (the "therefore" press).** The text says "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The "therefore" (*dio*) sits in the same verse as the coming and the overshadowing. In Acts 1:8 the result of the Holy Ghost coming upon the apostles is that they are "witnesses". In Luke 1:35 the result is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The result differs in each verse, so the verse decides.

**Luke 9:34, Hebrews 1:5, 2 Samuel 7:14, 1 Chronicles 28:6.**
- I grant that the verb in Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them", is the presence of God (*episkiazō*, G1982, "to invest with preternatural influence"). That is my point: God's presence is at the conceiving.
- I grant that Hebrews 1:5 applies "I will be to him a Father" to Christ.
- 1 Chronicles 28:6 reads "Solomon thy son", and "thy" is David's. For Christ, Matthew 1:20 gives "of the Holy Ghost" with Joseph named as "thy wife"'s husband.

## LINK 4: NARROWED TO: Joseph is father in the household and by naming, and "supposed" in Luke 3:23. The verb does not by itself carry a verdict of error.

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". Acts 14:19: "supposing he had been dead".
- **[L2]** *nomizō* (G3543, "properly to do by law (usage)... by extension, to deem or regard"; sheet: "suppose, thing, be wont") has both senses. Acts 16:13 uses "be wont".
- **[L3]** Acts 7:25: "For he supposed his brethren would have understood... but they understood not." Luke 1:35, in Luke's own voice, gives the Holy Ghost as the source of "that holy thing which shall be born of thee".
- **[L4]** Resting on Luke 3:23, Acts 14:19 [L1], *nomizō* [L2] and Acts 7:25, Luke 1:35 [L3]:
  - The challenger's "custom" sense is one of the verb's senses.
  - Elsewhere in Luke's writings the other sense stands with a supposition that does not stand (Acts 7:25, 14:19).
  - Here the word stands in a parenthesis and Luke's own earlier narration already gives the source.

**Luke 2:48 and John 6:42.** I grant that Mary says "thy father and I" and that Luke 2:41 and 2:27 say "parents". *patēr* (G3962) is glossed "father, parent". The household word is true of the man who is "the husband of Mary" (Matthew 1:16) and who "called his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:25). John 6:42 is the speech of the people ("whose father and mother we know"), and the next words they say show they are not weighing a begetting.

## LINK 5: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:22-23, with 1:18, place "a virgin" with child at the finding of the pregnancy. I withdraw the claim that the span of 1:25 covers the conception.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:22: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet". Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son".
- **[L3]** Genesis 24:16: "a virgin, neither had any man known her". Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child".
- **[L4]** Resting on Matthew 1:22-23 [L1] and Genesis 24:16 and Matthew 1:18 [L3]:
  - In the KJV's own use, "a virgin" is one whom no man has known.
  - Matthew says "all this was done" for the fulfilment, and puts the finding with child before the coming together.

**Isaiah 7:16, 8:3-4, 8:8.** Isaiah 8:3 gives a different child with a different name: "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz". Isaiah 7:14 gives the name "Immanuel". I grant that "Immanuel" is spoken in Isaiah 8:8 and that the boundary language of 7:16 returns at 8:4. Matthew 1:22 still says it was "done... that it might be fulfilled".

**Genesis 4:25 and 16:15.** I grant that these seeds have named fathers. They are not the link.

## LINK 6: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:16 and Luke 3:23 name different fathers for Joseph, and "made" in Romans 1:3 is the verb of Galatians 4:4. I hold Mary's Davidic flesh as an inference from these, not as stated.

I withdrew Luke 1:27 as a plain statement of her descent, and I withdraw nothing further.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary". Luke 3:23: "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli". Luke 3:31: "which was [the son] of Nathan, which was [the son] of David". Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh".
- **[L2]** *ginomai* (G1096, "to become, be made") is in Romans 1:3 and in Galatians 4:4.
- **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law". Ezra 2:61: "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name". Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel".
- **[L4]** Resting on Matthew 1:16, Luke 3:23 [L1] and Ezra 2:61 [L3]:
  - Joseph has one father in Matthew (Jacob) and another in Luke (Heli).
  - Ezra 2:61 shows a man reckoned under his wife's father's name.
  - The flesh "made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) is by Romans 1:3 "of the seed of David".

**Ezra 2:62.** I grant that those priests were put from the priesthood. That concerns the priestly register, and Hebrews 7:14 says of Christ's tribe that "Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood".

**Loins.** Hebrews 7:5 says the sons of Levi "come out of the loins of Abraham". *osphys* ("loins") there covers descendants through many mothers.

**Luke 2:4, 1:36, 1:5.** I grant that Luke 2:4 gives Joseph the house of David. I grant that Luke 1:36 gives Mary the kinswoman Elisabeth, "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5). I do not rest the link on either.

# CLOSE ROUND: DEFENDER

I keep D1 to D6 as declared. I narrow nothing and concede nothing. Below, the two listed witnesses come first, then the challenger's link-round presses by their C numbers.

## The two unanswered witnesses

**ANSWER: Luke 2:33 -- D4 --** "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him."

- **[L1]** Luke 2:33 puts Joseph beside "his mother" as one who "marvelled" at what was spoken of the child. This is the household in which Joseph stands as parent.
- **[L2]** The household word is *patēr* (G3962, "a 'father' (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)"). The lexicon's range is near or remote, literal or figurative. It is that word which Mary uses in Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing".
- **[L3]** Luke 2:27 has "the parents brought in the child Jesus", and Luke 2:41 has "his parents went to Jerusalem every year". Luke 2:49 then has the child's answer: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- **[L4]** D4 claims household and reckoned fatherhood, not begetting. The challenger presses Luke 2:33 as if "parents" names a begetter. The footing is Luke 2:48 [L1] with *patēr* "near or more remote ... figuratively" [L2]. Mary's "thy father" is answered in the next verse by the child's "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49 [L3]). The household word is used, and the child at once names another Father. So Luke 2:33 fits D4 and does not overturn it.

**ANSWER: John 1:45 -- D4 --** "Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."

- **[L1]** The words are Philip's speech. He names the child by his town ("of Nazareth") and his household ("the son of Joseph"), as a means of identifying him.
- **[L2]** *huios* (G5207, "a 'son' ... used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship"). The word's own gloss covers figurative kinship, so it does not fix begetting.
- **[L3]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" The speakers give what they know. The next words, "I came down from heaven", are the claim they are answering.
- **[L4]** In John 1:45 [L1] the same sentence ties "the son of Joseph" to the one "of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write". In John 6:42 [L3] "whose father and mother we know" is set against "I came down from heaven". The people's "son of Joseph" is the name by which he is known in the town. It sits beside, and does not cancel, Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" (see C4 below).

## D1: Matthew 1:16, begat and born (answering C3, P3.1)

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080): "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". The challenger granted that the text gives the father's place with "begat" and the mother's place with "of".
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2, "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". Matthew 1:6, "David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias". In 1:6 the father still "begat" and the woman stands in "of".
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:2 and 1:6 [L1/L3] show that every father in the line "begat", and the mothers come in with "of". At the last link the text reads "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary", and then "of whom was born Jesus". The verb "begat" is not carried to Joseph for Jesus. The woman is the "of whom". The challenger's own grant, that "begat" is the father's place, therefore meets a line whose final birth is given through the woman, with Joseph named "the husband of Mary" (*anēr*, G435, "husband"). D1 stands.

## D2: knowing before the taking (answering C2, P2.1 to P2.3)

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** *synerchomai* (G4905, "to convene ... or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)"). *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") in Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man".
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife" is said among those to be stoned.
- **[L4]** The challenger moves the knowing of Genesis 4:1 into the espousal. The footing against this is Matthew 1:18 [L1], where the finding is dated "before they came together", with *synerchomai* naming conjugal cohabitation [L2]. Deuteronomy 22:24 [L3] sets "humbled his neighbour's wife" under stoning. Joseph is "a just man" and "not willing to make her a publick example" (Matthew 1:19). So the text gives no place in the espousal for a knowing by Joseph. It gives "put her away privily" as his intent on finding her with child. Mary's "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" (Luke 1:34) uses present *ginōskō*, and the answer names no man at all (see D3). D2 stands.

## D3: the source of the conceiving (answering C1, C2 P2.3, and 1 John 5:1)

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]". Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) is the verb behind the margin "begotten". The begetting in Mary is "of the Holy Ghost". *dio* (G1352, "therefore") stands in Luke 1:35 itself, immediately after the Holy Ghost and the power.
- **[L3]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me".
- **[L4]** The challenger takes "born of God" in 1 John 5:1 to put the same origin on men with fathers. John 1:13 [L3] defines that "of God" as set "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man", and the lexicon calls this sense "figuratively, to regenerate" (G1080) [L2]. So the "of God" of believers is the regenerating sense. It is not a begetting that sits beside a human begetter. In Matthew 1:20 [L1] the margin "begotten" puts the begetting itself "of the Holy Ghost". In Luke 1:35 the "therefore also" falls in the same verse as the Holy Ghost and the power. Luke 1:35 answers "How shall this be?" (*pōs*, "in what way ... (by) what manner (means)", Luke 1:34) with the Holy Ghost and power, and names no man. Hebrews 10:5 gives the body "prepared". D3 stands.

## D4: Luke 3:23 (answering C4 and Acts 16:13)

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli". Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made".
- **[L2]** *nomizō* (G3543): "properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard: suppose, thing, be wont".
- **[L3]** Acts 14:19: "supposing he had been dead". Acts 7:25: "he supposed his brethren would have understood ... but they understood not".
- **[L4]** The challenger holds that the verb carries both law/usage and deeming. On either sense the sonship is reckoned (law, custom or deeming), and none of the glosses in G3543 is begetting. That is D4. With Acts 14:19 and 7:25 [L3] the supposing is of a thing that proved not so. With Acts 16:13 [L1] the "wont" is a custom. Luke 3:23 sets "as was supposed" before "the son of Joseph". Luke's narrated "parents" (Luke 2:27, 2:41) are the household term, answered by Luke 2:49. D4 stands.

## D5 and the Heli question (answering C5)

- **[L1]** Ezra 2:62: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found". Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary".
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) is the begetting verb that gives Matthew's line "Jacob" for Joseph.
- **[L3]** Ezra 2:61 records one man "called after their name", that is, after the name of his wife's father's house. Matthew 1:12 and Luke 3:27 both name Salathiel and Zorobabel.
- **[L4]** The challenger grants Jacob in Matthew and Heli in Luke. Luke 3:23 [L1] sets Heli's name on "Joseph" under the supposed sonship, and Matthew 1:16 [L1] gives the begetting father Jacob. The two names for Joseph's father are in the text, and neither answers the question about Jesus. Luke 3:23's "as was supposed" governs the whole row, including the "[the son] of Heli" that follows. D5's claim is not touched. Matthew 1:22 and 1:23, "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son", set the virgin conceiving beside the register's "of whom was born Jesus".

## D6 and C6 (the sign of Elisabeth)

- **[L1]** Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age ... who was called barren". Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- **[L2]** *dynamis* (G1411, "force ... miraculous power") and *eperchomai* (G1904, "to supervene ... (figuratively) influence") stand in Luke 1:35.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". Luke 1:34: "seeing I know not a man".
- **[L4]** The sign of verse 36 is given after the answer of verse 35. It shows God doing what is "impossible" (verse 37). For Elisabeth the impossible was age and barrenness, with her husband named in 1:13. For Mary the question was "seeing I know not a man" (1:34). Her answer names the Holy Ghost and the power and names no husband. The challenger grants the order (answer, then sign) and grants that "also" links the two. The "also" sets the two conceivings side by side as instances of what God can do. It does not turn Mary's answer into Elisabeth's.

## Final statement of D6

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost [conceived: Gr. begotten]", and Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man".
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, begotten), and *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know").
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:16, "of whom was born Jesus"; Luke 3:23, "(as was supposed) the son of Joseph"; Luke 2:49, "my Father's business".
- **[L4]** D1 to D5 stand on the footing above. The begetting in Mary is "of the Holy Ghost". The line names Joseph "the husband of Mary" and not the begetter. The child answers Mary's "thy father" with "my Father's business". Christ had no biological father. Joseph was his father by marriage and reckoning, as Luke's "(as was supposed)" holds.
